public_rationale: The ordinary reading is supported for the United States. Gallup found a nine-point increase in Gen Z anger and a fourteen-point decline in excitement. Quinnipiac found an eleven-point increase in adults expecting AI to harm their daily lives. These substantial year-over-year changes support growing backlash by May. Infrastructure opposition also increased, although it is an imperfect proxy. Stable use and largely unchanged trust qualify the claim without overturning it.
limitations: Growing fast has no stated numerical threshold.
The evidence establishes recent year-over-year deterioration, not acceleration over the few days before publication.
The geographic interpretation materially affects the assessment.

statement.excerpt: As I am sure you have heard by now, the backlash against AI i keep nattering on about is growing fast.
statement.document_title: Could generative AI turn out to be the tech industry’s Vietnam? And could public backlash lead AI to a better place?

our_interpretation: The plain reading is a substantial recent increase in negative public sentiment or active opposition to AI.
The surrounding examples concern American students and politics, so the principal scope is the United States.
I assess early 2026 through the post date against earlier comparable observations. Marcus supplies neither a numerical growth threshold nor a comparison interval.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable polling shows a substantial recent deterioration in attitudes toward AI, with documented public opposition providing corroboration.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable, broadly representative evidence shows attitudes and opposition remaining stable or becoming substantially more favorable during the relevant period.

evidence.locator: Opening paragraph; Negative Sentiment About AI Has Increased; Survey Methods
evidence.explanation: The survey ending March 4 found Gen Z anger rising from 22% to 31% over a year, while excitement fell 14 percentage points. These are substantial changes, although weekly use remained essentially stable.

The national adult survey found expected harm to daily life rising from 44% in April 2025 to 55%, corroborating worsening sentiment beyond Gen Z. However, its trust measure was largely unchanged, so deterioration was not uniform across measures.

evidence.locator: Paragraph following the canceled-project investment totals
evidence.explanation: Heatmap counted at least 20 cancellations following local opposition in the first quarter, compared with roughly 25 during all of 2025. This corroborates growing infrastructure opposition, but the article explicitly includes facilities not intended to run AI models.
